transcript: I'm going to teach you more in the next 60 seconds about the thyroid than most board certified endocrinologists ever explain. Not to attack anyone, but to give you clarity. The thyroid sits here quietly in your neck. It produces T4 and T3, but here is what most people never hear. The thyroid only produces a small portion of active T3 directly. Most of your active thyroid hormone is created through conversion inside the body. So if T3 is low, why do we immediately blame the thyroid? If a detective saw 20% evidence in one place and 80% somewhere else, where would he investigate first? T4 must convert into T3. That process depends on nutrients, on B vitamins, on methylation, on stress levels, on how safe your nervous system feels. When conversion slows, medication is often increased, but sometimes the gland is not broken, sometimes the body is missing support, the body is intelligent, it wants to function. Give it the raw materials, reduce stress, restore balance. There is no stronger hormone than the one your body creates naturally. The thyroid was never the enemy, imbalance was. Follow for more wisdom like this.
